topics.description: The Nazi extermination camp in occupied Poland that operated as part of Operation Reinhard and was located near the village of Treblinka.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: After the destruction of this city, so-called “Robinson Crusoes” hid in its ruins for over three  months. Groups such as the ZOB, which operated a bunker at Miła (MEE-wah) 18, fought Jürgen  (YORG-en) Stroop's forces in this city. A forest near this city was the site of a facility built under  Operation Reinhard in the village of (*) Treblinka (treb-LINK-ah). Chłodna (WOHD-noh) Street was  an enclave within this city, which in 1939 had the largest Jewish population in Europe. For 10 points,  name this Polish city where Jews launched a 1943 uprising against the Nazis from a designated ghetto.

topics.description: The German steel combat helmet introduced in 1916, recognized for its distinctive coal-scuttle shape and extensive use in wartime propaganda.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One of these objects designed in 1915 by Louis Adrian [loo-ee ay-dree-un] had a distinct ridge at the top and was adopted by the French Army. Another of them designed by John Leopold Brodie was nicknamed the “doughboy” by American soldiers. Frederick William IV designed one of these objects made of boiled leather, called the Pickelhaube [pickle-how-buh], which had a (*) distinctive upward spike. In 1916 Germany introduced a steel type of these objects whose “coal scuttle” shape was widely used in propaganda. This worn piece of equipment protected soldiers from falling shrapnel during World War I. For 10 points, name this piece of armor worn on the head.
parts.answer: World War I helmets [accept Adrian helmets or Brodie helmets or Stahlhelme]

topics.description: A Roman author, naturalist, and military commander who died during the 79 CE eruption of Mount Vesuvius.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Spartacus led a slave rebellion which rappelled down this mountain to win a battle. The ancient city of Herculaneum was located near this mountain. Pliny the Elder died during a natural disaster caused by this (*) volcano, whose eruption buried an ancient Roman city in volcanic ash, preserving it. For 10 points, name this volcano which destroyed Pompeii.

topics.description: The deliberate killing or attempted killing of a political leader or other prominent public figure, often for ideological or political purposes.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Alberto Fernandez declared September 2nd a national holiday following a failed one of these events in Argentina. Perceived ties to the Unification Church were used as justification for one of these events. DEA agents were impersonated during one of these events in 2021 which led to the arrests of at least 21 (*) Colombian ex-militants. One of these events was an attempt to carry out a fatwa on Salman Rushdie. In July 2022, a jury-rigged shotgun was used to perform one of these events during a speech in Nara Prefecture. For 10 points, name these events that killed Jovenel Moise and Shinzo Abe.
parts.answer: assassinations [or attempted assassinations; accept murders; accept assassination attempts; prompt on shootings or stabbings]

topics.description: A British mining magnate and imperialist who founded De Beers and served as prime minister of the Cape Colony in the 1890s.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A “Great” city that shares its name with this country was home to the Eastern Enclosure, where six  soapstone sculptures were found. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this country, where long-time dictator Robert Mugabe died in 2019.

parts.label: B
parts.question: A short-lived republic that became Zimbabwe was named after this founder of De Beers Diamond  Company, who was prime minister of the Cape Colony in the 1890s.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The builders of Great Zimbabwe were ancestors of this present-day Bantu people, who formed the  Kingdom of Mutapa (moo-TAP-uh) under Nyatsimba (nee-AHT-sim-bah).

topics.description: A period of authoritarian rule in India from 1975 to 1977 marked by censorship, political arrests, forced sterilization campaigns, and the suspension of civil liberties.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This leader’s slogan “eradicate poverty” was mocked as “eradicate the poor” amidst this leader’s “urban renewal” which saw the destruction of the Turkmen Gate. This leader conducted the Smiling Buddha nuclear bomb tests at Pokhran. During this leader’s tenure, the Anandpur Resolution evolved into the demands of the (*) Khalistan movement. This leader’s son oversaw mandatory vasectomies after a third child during a period called the Emergency. After ordering the destruction of the Golden Temple at Amritsar, this daughter of Jawaharlal Nehru was assassinated by her Sikh bodyguards. For 10 points, name this only female prime minister of India.
parts.answer: Indira Gandhi [prompt on Gandhi; reject “Rajiv Gandhi”; reject “Mohandas Gandhi” or “Mahatma Gandhi”]

topics.description: An armored Joseon Korean warship, traditionally associated with Admiral Yi Sun-sin and used against Japanese invasions during the Imjin War.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about Admiral Yi Sun-sin, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Admiral Yi led the navy of Joseon Korea against the invading forces of this Japanese leader, a “Great Unifier” who was succeeded by Tokugawa Ieyasu.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Toyotomi Hideyoshi [accept Hashiba Hideyoshi; accept any underlined part and names in either order]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Admiral Yi invented a type of warship named after this animal, whose deck was covered in hexagonal armor plates and studded with iron spikes.
parts.answer: ANSWER: turtle ship [or gwiseon; or geobukseon]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Admiral Yi’s ships supplemented their cannons with devices known as hwachas which launched these projectiles using rockets. They are more commonly fired from a bow.

topics.description: Gaelic denotes the Goidelic languages and associated cultural traditions of Ireland and Scotland, especially as promoted by the Gaelic Revival.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Douglas Hyde and Patrick Pearse were members of a League founded in 1893 to promote a language known by  this term. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this cultural term, which underwent a “revival” in the late 1800s that opposed English influence in  Ireland. This term refers to Irish and Scottish culture before English invasions.
parts.answer: Gaelic [accept Gaeilge; or the Gaelic Revival; prompt on Irish or Celtic]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Gaelic League was centered on this city, which became the capital of Ireland.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Celtic culture spread as far as this country after the ancient Galatians settled down. This country warred with  Greece after World War I under its leader, Mustafa Kemal Ataturk.

topics.description: Ancient Mediterranean pirates from Cilicia who raided ships, participated in the slave trade, and were defeated by Pompey after kidnapping Julius Caesar.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Because this island was considered the birthplace of Artemis and Apollo, its residents were prohibited from dying and tainting the land, so prisoners were executed on nearby Mykonos. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this island in the Cyclades which hosted the Athenian treasury and thus lent its name to Athens’ alliance of city-states.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Delos’s importance as a port waned after it was sacked by this king of Pontus who fought the Romans in Anatolia. This ruler allegedly developed a method of ingesting non-lethal amounts of poison to build immunity.
parts.answer: Mithridates VI Eupator [or Mithridates the Great; accept Mithridatism]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Delos was a slave trading hub for groups of these people from Cilicia who later kidnapped Julius Caesar. Pompey waged war against these people who attack and raid ships at sea.

topics.description: An ancient Mesoamerican civilization known for colossal stone heads, including those found at San Lorenzo and La Venta.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A 2022 wildfire damaged many of these sculptures in the Rano Raraku crater. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name or describe these rock figures that were created by the Rapa Nui people on Easter Island.
parts.answer: moai (accept descriptions of large stone heads; prompt on description of human sculptures, as some of the heads feature torsos)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Large stone heads are a common motif in historical art. This Mesoamerican civilization, which invented a ball game popular in later cultures, carved large heads out of boulders in cities like La Venta.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Several Persian and Greek gods are depicted in massive stone heads on Mount Nemrut, which is in this modern-day country. A decidedly older ancient ruin in this country, C¸ atalhoy¨ uk¨ [chat-ull-HOY-ook], dates to nearly 10,000 years ago.
